9001.name: hoai_adventure_1_play
9001.longInstructions:
Play **{{title}}** and {{goal}}.

The game only understands a few commands. Type `help` to see them, then {{goalTask}}.

Stuck? Go `{{toSecond}}` and `talk to {{npc}}`.

You're done when {{doneWhen}}.
9001.teacherMarkdown:
- What parts of this story came from the world's rules, and what parts came from the player?
- Does choosing an action make the player an author? Why or why not?

9002.name: hoai_adventure_2_look_inside
9002.longInstructions:
The first room mentions a {{detail}}. Type `examine {{detail}}`.

Then click the command you typed—it is a button—to open **How it was understood** and see where the game lost track of your words.

You're done once you've tried the {{detailShort}} and looked inside that command.
9002.teacherMarkdown:
- Who caused this failure: the player, the command reader, or the world author?
- When a story names something, what does it promise the player can do?

validations.message: You found the gap between the words and the world.
Now click the command you typed to see why the game didn't understand it.

9006.name: hoai_adventure_6_meet_the_ai
9006.longInstructions:
Turn on the AI: pick a model from the **Interpreter** menu at the top right and wait for it to load.

Type a normal sentence that means a game command, like `can you grab the {{toolShort}} for me`.

Then ask for something the game cannot do, like `fly to the moon`. A careful AI asks you a question. A careless one guesses a command you never asked for. Watch which one yours does.

You are done when the AI has understood one request, and has asked or guessed at another.
9006.teacherMarkdown:
- Did the AI change the world, or only translate the player's words into a command?
- When the AI guessed instead of asking, what did it do? Would that be acceptable in an app that matters?
- When the AI asks a question, who is shaping the next line of the story?

validations.message: The AI asked a question when it was not sure. That is the careful choice.
The AI guessed. The game cannot do what you asked, so it picked a command you never typed. Look at what it did.
Now ask for something the game cannot do, like flying to the moon, and watch for a question.

9007.name: hoai_adventure_7_ai_dial
9007.longInstructions:
The room you start in mentions a {{detail}} the author never built. Try the same command with the **AI dial**, beside the game, at different settings and watch what changes.

The {{detailShort}} never becomes a real object: the AI can write words, not rules. Improvise lets characters say things the author never wrote.

**Invent** is locked—use what happened in the game to debate why.
9007.teacherMarkdown:
- At which dial setting does the AI begin to share authorship, if any? Why?
- Why might inventing events be locked even when improvising is available?
- Who is responsible when AI-written story text conflicts with a world rule?
- Did a line marked **AI wrote this** ever say something that was not true in the game? How could a player tell?

validations.message: Your AI boundary is set. Be ready to explain it.

steps.text: If you have not already, choose a model from the **Interpreter** menu at the top right and wait for it to load.
Set the dial to **Off** and type `examine the {{detailShort}}`.
Still on **Off**, type `{{understandPhrase}}`. Then set the dial to **Understand** and type it again. Which setting worked out what you meant?
Set the dial to **Fill gaps** and type `examine the {{detailShort}}` again. Notice the line marked **AI wrote this**.

Set the dial to **Improvise**, go `{{toSecond}}` to the {{secondRoom}}, and type `ask the {{npc}} about {{askAbout}}`. Notice the {{npc}} answers with a line marked **AI wrote this**—a line the author never wrote. Is what it says true in the game? Check with `look` and `inventory`.
Pick the setting you want for your game. Add a tone and theme if you like, write your reason, and press **Save my setting**.

9003.name: hoai_adventure_3_name_the_mug
9003.displayName: If you name it, answer it
9003.longInstructions:
The AI could write words about the {{detail}}, but you still could not pick it up. Only the author can make it real, and you are the author now.

In **Add a thing**, write what a player sees when they examine the {{detail}}. Then press **Add it to the world**.

Type `examine {{detailShort}}`. You are done when the game answers with the words you wrote. Try `take {{detailShort}}` too.

Then think like a player: what else might they call it? Add those words to **Also called**, press **Save changes**, and try them.
9003.teacherMarkdown:
- The AI described the {{detail}} and the student built it. What is different about the two?
- How did one short form change which player actions were possible?
- Who should decide what is true in a story: the author, the player, or the AI?

validations.message: The {{detailShort}} is real now: it is in the rules, not only in the words.
The {{detailShort}} is in the world. Now examine it in the game.

9009.name: hoai_adventure_9_real_life
9009.displayName: Set the dial for real life
9009.longInstructions:
The dial is not only for games. Anyone who builds an app with AI has to decide how much the AI may do.

Here are three apps. For each one, pick where you would set the dial and write why.

There is no single right answer, so be ready to defend yours. You are done when all three have a setting and a reason.
9009.teacherMarkdown:
- Where did the class disagree most? What made that app different from the others?
- For each app, what could go wrong at the highest setting, and who would be harmed?
- Who should get to set the dial: the people who build the app, the people who use it, or someone else?
- Name an app you use that has AI in it. Where do you think its dial is set?

validations.message: You set all three. Be ready to explain what made them different.

scenarios.title: A homework helper
scenarios.blurb: An app that helps students with their math homework.

options.off: No AI. It shows the worked examples from the textbook.
options.understand: The AI works out what you are asking, then shows the explanation your teacher wrote.
options.fill_gaps: The AI writes a hint when your teacher did not write one.
options.improvise: The AI chats with you like a tutor, in its own words.
options.invent: The AI decides whether your answer is right and gives you the grade.

scenarios.title: A clinic app
scenarios.blurb: An app people use to ask a clinic about their medicine.

options.off: No AI. It shows the label the pharmacist wrote.
options.understand: The AI works out which medicine you mean, then shows the pharmacist's instructions.
options.fill_gaps: The AI writes an answer when the pharmacist's notes do not cover your question.
options.improvise: The AI talks with you about how you feel, in its own words.
options.invent: The AI decides how much medicine you should take.

scenarios.title: A story game for your friends
scenarios.blurb: A text adventure you wrote, like the one you just played.

options.off: No AI. Players type exact commands.
options.understand: The AI works out what players mean. Your rules decide what happens.
options.fill_gaps: The AI describes details you did not write.
options.improvise: The AI makes up what your characters say.
options.invent: The AI makes up new events in your story.
